mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-51.0 to -33.9), reflecting a steady recovery trend; absent a shock, this week-on-week improvement is expected to continue, producing a higher 4-week mean relative to the prior 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -51.0 to -33.9 over three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If the 4-week forward mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the trailing 4-week mean despite the observed 3-week upward momentum, the momentum-continuation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, continued easing of workplace restrictions (WORKPLACES improving from -38.6 to -24.9) signals policy-driven relaxation that will further lift RETAIL_REC over the next 2 weeks as commuters resume shopping trips tied to work schedules.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -38.6 to -24.9 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks even though WORKPLACES continues to improve by more than 5 points per week, the policy-linkage mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp single-week drop in PARKS (-6.4 to -24.1) indicates a sudden behavioral pullback from outdoor activity, likely due to weather or a local event, which commonly coincides with reduced discretionary retail trips in the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -6.4 to -24.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following a PARKS drop exceeding 15 points, the behavioral pullback mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both show sustained recovery simultaneously, the combined restoration of commuting infrastructure and employment activity amplifies RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series alone would predict, because commuters pick up retail errands on transit routes.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -51.9 to -37.0 and WORKPLACES from -38.6 to -24.9 concurrently
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean does not exceed its trailing mean despite joint sustained improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The decline in PARKS during Southern Hemisphere winter (June) reflects seasonal weather suppression of outdoor recreation rather than reduced overall mobility; since indoor retail and recreation activities are weather-resilient, RETAIL_REC is expected to remain stable or improve over the next 2 weeks despite falling PARKS.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2020-06-15 falls within Southern Hemisphere winter
fact:PARKS fell to -24.1 while RETAIL_REC continued improving to -33.9
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC declines over the next 2 weeks in tandem with the PARKS seasonal drop, the decoupling hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has steadily declined from 20.7 to 13.6 over the snapshot, indicating people are spending progressively less time at home; this reduced home-dwelling behavior directly frees time for out-of-home retail and recreation visits in the immediate following week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 20.7 to 13.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a continued decline in RESIDENTIAL, the time-reallocation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, GROCERY_PHARM mobility stabilizing near its pre-pandemic baseline (currently -5.7, oscillating within a narrow band) signals that essential-trip patterns have normalized; this normalization typically precedes broader convergence of RETAIL_REC toward baseline over the subsequent 4 weeks as discretionary shopping resumes.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within +/-6 points of baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM oscillated between -6.0 and -1.0 across the snapshot weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean fails to rise despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable near baseline, the normalization-convergence mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovery stalls (week-on-week change near zero) while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated relative to baseline, this combination signals persistent caution about leaving home via public transport, which suppresses RETAIL_REC growth over the next 2 weeks even if other indicators improve.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change is within +/-2 points while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT changed only from -37.3 to -37.0 in the latest week while RESIDENTIAL stayed at 13.6
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks despite stalled TRANSIT recovery and elevated RESIDENTIAL, the caution-suppression interaction mechanism is rejected.
